newsitem.title: USA: Hundreds donate blood for Malcolm X widow.
newsitem.headline: Hundreds donate blood for Malcolm X widow.

text.p: Hundreds of people lined up at a Harlem bank on Monday to donate blood for the widow of civil rights leader Malcolm X, severely burned in a fire allegedly set by her troubled grandson.
Just a few hours after the blood drive for Betty Shabazz began at the Carver Federal Savings Bank, 320 donors already had given blood, bank officials said.
"It's such a phenomenal outpouring of people," said Valli Sheppard-Vess, the bank's human resources chief and head of the drive. "It's great for Betty. People just keep coming and coming."
Hospital technicians had to quadruple the number of cots to 16 to accommodate the unexpected number of donors, she said. More than 300 people were outside the bank when the drive began.

Shabazz, 63, suffered third-degree burns over 80 percent of her body in a fire at her Yonkers, New York, apartment on June 1. A third-degree burn is one that extends deep into the skin's underlying tissue.
She is in critical but stable condition at New York's Jacobi Hospital. Shabazz has undergone four operations to repair burned tissue.
A Jacobi Hospital spokeswoman said Shabazz needed "quite a bit of blood" because the severe burn means she is suffering a steady loss of fluids.
Surgeons have removed 72 percent of her burned tissue. A fifth operation is set for Wednesday, the spokeswoman said.
Surgeons have replaced her charred skin with Integra, an artifical skin product. The material lets the inner layer of her skin heal enough to accept a permanent skin graft later.
Malcolm Shabazz, 12, named after his grandfather, Malcolm X, is alleged to have splashed gasoline at the door of his grandmother's apartment and set it afire.
Shabazz's nylon nightgown caught fire when she tried to put out the blaze. The boy allegedly thought his grandmother's death would hasten his return to Texas, where his mother lives in San Antonio.
He is being held at a juvenile facility awaiting his next date in Family Court.
